title: Anonymous guest chat with Maya
why: Three rows: an in-memory anonymous session manager (`S-705`), its edge route mapping (`S-704`), and a row that records the absent front-end (`S-723`). The capability is attested by the production inventory, not verifiable from this repository — `S-705` carries its own evidence caveat that the module is ABSENT from this checkout (conflict C4), and `ai администратор/site_guest_chat.py` is indeed not in the evidence tree. About the front-end, only one thing is proven: the shipped marketing bundle `сайт и приложение/index.html` (870237 bytes) contains `site_guest_chat` 0 and `me_visitor` 0 — absence from one bundle, not absence in production. `S-723` states in terms that it is NOT safe to conclude the front-end exists nowhere, because the sibling community UI behind the same proxy ships as a deployed Next.js chunk with no source here (conflict C3). All three rows carry `canonicalOwner` "- (no capability named on the inventory row)" with source REQUIRES SIGNATURE, so the owner line is what the signature creates, not something the inventory already states. Attributing it now is what keeps it from being rediscovered later as a new feature.
disappear: Nothing. No row here is retired: `S-704` and `S-723` are OUT OF SCOPE WITH EXACT REASON and both carry "NOT RETIRED - out of scope, with the reason on the row", and `S-705` is KEEP AS CHAT SURFACE, "NOT RETIRED - it is the conversation".
remain: The anonymous session manager as the conversation itself — chat carries it, no separate surface is required — and with it the discipline `S-705` names: it renders under the TEXT_ONLY conformance reference (R1), and because the principal is an unauthenticated stranger the envelope must carry ZERO COMMIT intents, since no widget type may by itself confer consent, booking authority, marketing permission, finance permission, tenant authority or approval, and the VerificationLevel floor (Gate 4) refuses them on channel identity regardless. The route mapping stays as one name inside the relay's seven-action, POST-only-else-405 allowlist with its own payload allowlist; Platform/channels §0 keeps `edge-relay` out of ChannelProfile, so a transport cannot declare presentation capability and the authority decision is made at the canonical owner. The missing front-end remains an OPEN item, not a settled design choice: `S-723` records a CAPABILITY GAP that "belongs in the missing-capability list, not the surface census", and no row calls the absence deliberate.
risk: LOW. Nothing is retired, re-pointed or re-parented, no client-facing behaviour moves, all three rows carry no parity risk note, two carry no package, and the parity requirement on the out-of-scope rows is "none - not this programme surface". The care is in the record rather than the change: approving this as attribution must not be read as a signed finding that the guest-chat front-end does not exist, because the repository can neither confirm nor refute that (C3, C4), and a signed "does not exist" is exactly what would authorise building a second guest-chat UI beside one that may already be deployed. The module's own existence likewise rests on the production inventory, so the owner line names a capability this checkout cannot show.
user_impact: No user notices anything, because nothing in this group is built, moved or retired — but it is not uniform "attribution over three rows". Two rows are OUT OF SCOPE WITH EXACT REASON, package "-": S-704, a route name in the relay's 7-action map (r09-site-community-proxy.php L4-9), and S-723, a front-end proven absent from the shipped bundle (index.html, 870237 bytes: site_guest_chat 0, me_visitor 0 — re-verified, and app.html likewise 0). The third, S-705 (site_guest_chat.py), is KEEP AS CHAT SURFACE inside package K5, so it carries a live conformance obligation — TEXT_ONLY parity (R1) and a zero-COMMIT envelope — not paperwork. Two evidence caveats belong on the signature, not under it. (1) S-705 is ABSENT from this checkout; its existence rests on the production inventory (conflict C4) — the owner is being attributed to a module the audited tree does not contain. (2) S-723 must not be signed as "the front-end does not exist" or as a "deliberate absence": its own row calls it a CAPABILITY GAP belonging in the missing-capability list, and states it is NOT safe to conclude the front-end exists nowhere — the sibling community UI for the same proxy ships as a deployed Next.js chunk on muzhskayaestetika.рф with no source here, so the guest-chat UI may be deployed the same way (C3, C4). An anonymous visitor therefore sees exactly whatever they see today, which the repository can neither confirm nor refute. The owner and staff are untouched because nothing changes — not because the surface is anonymous-only: the same relay file also carries site_event_moderation and site_event_resolve, which site_community.py gates on database.is_admin. The guest-chat path itself does create no Client or User record (in-memory sessions only, no DB write) — that part holds.
security_impact: NO CHANGE IN EITHER DIRECTION — nothing is removed and nothing is added; that much holds. The verified relay facts hold too: the 7-action allowlist, POST-only else 405 (L10-14), the HMAC-signed me_visitor cookie (L21-33), and `network` derived from REMOTE_ADDR, never X-Forwarded-For (L42-43). Per S-704 the allowlist is hardening, not an authority path, and this group does not move the authority decision — though note the canonical owner it "stays at" is the thing being signed: all three rows read canonicalOwner "- (no capability named)" / REQUIRES SIGNATURE. Three corrections to the forward-looking claim, which as written overstates protection. (1) Wrong gate: F11 fixes Gate 4 as Tenant scope and Gate 5 as the Verification floor, and erratum E-3 rewrites "Gate 4 as the floor comparison" to Gate 5 — S-705's rationale carries the old error and the contract overrides it. (2) Wrong rung: a marketing-site stranger resolves to ANONYMOUS (rank 0, no principal resolved), not CHANNEL_IDENTITY (rank 1, which requires a known channel subject — a Telegram chat id or push endpoint — that this visitor does not have); the refusal is EFFECT_FLOOR['COMMIT'] = SESSION_VERIFIED against an ANONYMOUS principal. (3) Not built: P-11 records the whole VerificationLevel ladder and verificationFloor() as [ABSENT] — all five rung tokens 0 hits repo-wide, verification_level/verificationLevel 0 — delivered by K2 (wave 1) and K4 (wave 2). So the floor refuses nothing today; it is a requirement, not a running control, and must not be written in the present tense. The contract's stronger, unmentioned term is that guest-chat is a named channel at tier ANONYMOUS_CHAT, max_intents 4, effect ceiling REFINE/HANDOFF only (§4.5.3) — a second independent subtraction at EP-FIT, also [TO BUILD], and per CH1 a ceiling is a maximum, never a permission. What actually fences the live surface today is in site_guest_chat.py: PUBLIC_TOOLS is a 7-member read-only frozenset with every other tool passed as disabled_tools, anonymizer.redact_pii bounces any PII-bearing message to a canned redirect, consent is not True returns 403, plus session/global concurrency caps and site_community.py's IP/day/global spend_limits. Two caveats on the relay's HMAC that the phrasing dresses as strength: the secret is config['bot_token'] — the Telegram bot token — shared across the visitor cookie, the visitor/network derivations, X-Site-Signature and the community form token; and `visitor` is an HMAC over the nonce inside the browser's own cookie, so it is unforgeable but rotatable at will. Neither is a regression here, since O02 changes nothing.
